data.name: Settings_LanguageSection
data.comment: Settings, General tab: section header. Written in capitals in English; write it as your language writes a heading.

data.name: Settings_Language
data.comment: Settings, General tab: the setting's name.

data.name: Settings_LanguageHint
data.value: Menus, dialogs and messages. SQL, server messages and your data stay as they are, and a string with no translation yet shows in English.
data.comment: Settings, General tab: under the Language setting.

data.name: Settings_LanguageSystem
data.comment: Settings, General tab: the first choice in the Language list, which follows the operating system. {language} is that language's name in itself, such as English or 简体中文.

data.name: Settings_TabGeneral
data.comment: Settings: name of the first tab.

data.name: Settings_TabAppearance
data.comment: Settings: name of the second tab.

data.name: Settings_TabEditor
data.comment: Settings: name of the third tab.

data.name: Settings_TabData
data.comment: Settings: name of the fourth tab.

data.name: Settings_StartupSection
data.comment: Settings, General tab: section heading. Written in capitals in English; write it as your language writes a heading.

data.name: Settings_AutoConnect
data.value: Open the last connection on startup
data.comment: Settings, General tab, Startup: the setting's name (a switch).

data.name: Settings_AutoConnectHint
data.value: Connects straight to whatever you used last instead of waiting at the connection dialog. The dialog is still one Switch connection away, and a failed connect lands back in it with the error.
data.comment: Settings, General tab, Startup: hint under the setting. "Switch connection" is the name of a menu command.

data.name: Settings_KeyboardSection
data.comment: Settings, General tab: section heading. Written in capitals in English; write it as your language writes a heading.

data.name: Settings_ShortcutModifier
data.comment: Settings, General tab, Keyboard: the setting's name.

data.name: Settings_ShortcutModifierHint
data.value: Auto uses Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Applies immediately to shortcuts, the command palette, and the cheat sheet.
data.comment: Settings, General tab, Keyboard: hint under the setting. Cmd and Ctrl are key names and stay as they are.

data.name: Settings_ModifierAuto
data.comment: Settings, General tab, Keyboard: a choice in the shortcut modifier list (pick Cmd or Ctrl by platform).

data.name: Settings_HistorySection
data.comment: Settings, General tab: section heading. Written in capitals in English; write it as your language writes a heading.

data.name: Settings_RecordHistory
data.comment: Settings, General tab, History: the setting's name (a switch).

data.name: Settings_RecordHistoryHint
data.value: Keeps the text of every query you run in a local file that is not encrypted. Passwords in statements are masked.
data.comment: Settings, General tab, History: hint under the setting.

data.name: Settings_Theme
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: the setting's name.

data.name: Settings_ThemeHint
data.value: System follows the OS light/dark setting
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: hint under Theme.

data.name: Settings_ThemeSystem
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: a choice in the Theme list, following the operating system's light or dark setting.

data.name: Settings_ThemeLight
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: a choice in the Theme list.

data.name: Settings_ThemeDark
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: a choice in the Theme list.

data.name: Settings_InterfaceFont
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: the setting's name.

data.name: Settings_InterfaceFontHint
data.value: System is San Francisco on macOS, Segoe UI on Windows and your desktop's font on Linux. Inter looks the same everywhere.
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: hint under Interface font. San Francisco, Segoe UI and Inter are font names and stay as they are; System is the first choice of the list.

data.name: Settings_FontSystem
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: a choice in the Interface font list, the operating system's own font.

data.name: Settings_CodeFont
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: the setting's name.

data.name: Settings_CodeFontHint
data.value: For the SQL editor, values, plans and every other place that shows code. Lists the monospace fonts installed on this computer.
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: hint under Code font.

data.name: Settings_CodeFontBuiltIn
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: the first choice in the Code font list, the font that ships with pgNimbus. JetBrains Mono is a font name and stays as it is.

data.name: Settings_EditorFontSize
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: the setting's name.

data.name: Settings_EditorFontSizeHint
data.value: The size every SQL editor starts at, and returns to on {gesture}. Zooming changes only the editor you are in.
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: hint under Editor font size. {gesture} is the keyboard shortcut that resets the zoom, such as Ctrl+0 or ⌘0; it is built by the app and not translated.

data.name: Settings_ShowSizes
data.value: Show relation sizes in the schema tree
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: the setting's name (a switch). A relation is a table or materialized view.

data.name: Settings_ShowSizesHint
data.value: Adds each table and materialized view's on-disk size (heap + indexes + TOAST) as a dim hint next to its name
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: hint under Show relation sizes. Heap and TOAST are PostgreSQL storage terms.

data.name: Settings_CompletionSection
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab: section heading. Written in capitals in English; write it as your language writes a heading.

data.name: Settings_AutoAlias
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab, Completion: the setting's name (a switch).

data.name: Settings_AutoAliasHint
data.value: Accepting a table after FROM/JOIN also inserts a short alias (orders → orders o)
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab, Completion: hint under the setting. FROM and JOIN are SQL keywords; the example is SQL.

data.name: Settings_KeywordCase
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab, Completion: the setting's name.

data.name: Settings_KeywordCaseHint
data.value: How accepted keywords are written. As typed follows what you started: tr gives true, SEL gives SELECT.
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab, Completion: hint under Keyword case. "As typed" is the first choice of the list; tr/true and SEL/SELECT are typing examples and stay as they are.

data.name: Settings_KeywordCaseAsTyped
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab: a choice in the Keyword case list; keywords follow the case the user started typing in.

data.name: Settings_KeywordCaseUpper
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab: a choice in the Keyword case list; keywords are written in capitals. Write it in capitals if your language has them.

data.name: Settings_KeywordCaseLower
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab: a choice in the Keyword case list; keywords are written in small letters.

data.name: Settings_AlwaysQualify
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab, Completion: the setting's name (a switch).

data.name: Settings_AlwaysQualifyHint
data.value: Off, a table goes in bare when the search_path finds it (customers), and with its schema otherwise (saas.users). On, every table goes in with its schema.
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab, Completion: hint under the setting. search_path is a PostgreSQL setting; customers and saas.users are examples and stay as they are.

data.name: Settings_EnterAccepts
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab, Completion: the setting's name (a switch).

data.name: Settings_EnterAcceptsHint
data.value: On, Enter takes a suggestion you picked or started typing, and is a newline otherwise. Off, only Tab accepts and Enter always ends the line.
data.comment: Settings, Editor tab, Completion: hint under the setting. Enter and Tab are key names.

data.name: Settings_SafeMode
data.comment: Settings, Data tab: the setting's name (a switch).

data.name: Settings_SafeModeHint
data.value: Grid edits, deletes, and Add-row inserts are staged locally and highlighted; review the generated SQL, then commit everything as one transaction — or discard
data.comment: Settings, Data tab: hint under Safe mode.

data.name: Settings_FilterBar
data.value: Always show the filter bar while browsing
data.comment: Settings, Data tab: the setting's name (a switch).

data.name: Settings_FilterBarHint
data.value: Keeps the filter line above the grid even with no conditions, so + Filter is always in reach. Off, it appears whenever a condition (or a WHERE you typed) filters the rows. Also toggled by the funnel in the status bar.
data.comment: Settings, Data tab: hint under the setting. "+ Filter" is the name of a button; WHERE is the SQL keyword.

data.name: Settings_BackupSection
data.comment: Settings, Data tab: section heading. Written in capitals in English; write it as your language writes a heading.

data.name: Settings_PgTools
data.comment: Settings, Data tab, Backup: the card's name.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsHint
data.value: pg_dump and pg_restore make and restore backups. pgNimbus finds them where PostgreSQL, pgAdmin, Postgres.app and Homebrew install them.
data.comment: Settings, Data tab, Backup: hint under the card's name. pg_dump, pg_restore, pgAdmin, Postgres.app and Homebrew are program names.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsChooseFolder
data.comment: Settings, Data tab, Backup: button that opens a folder picker.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsChooseFolderTip
data.value: Pick the folder that holds pg_dump and pg_restore
data.comment: Settings, Data tab, Backup: tooltip of the Choose Folder button.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsLookAgain
data.comment: Settings, Data tab, Backup: button that searches for the programs again.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsAutomatic
data.comment: Settings, Data tab, Backup: button that goes back to searching automatically.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsAutomaticTip
data.value: Forget the folder and search again
data.comment: Settings, Data tab, Backup: tooltip of the Automatic button.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsLooking
data.comment: Status line while the search runs, in Settings and in the Backup and Restore windows. {tool} is the program name: pg_dump or pg_restore.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsFromFolder
data.comment: Settings, Data tab, Backup: line under the card when the user picked a folder. {folder} is a folder path.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsFoundAutomatically
data.comment: Settings, Data tab, Backup: line under the card when the programs were found without the user choosing a folder.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsNeeds
data.comment: Heading of the Backup and Restore windows when no usable program is installed. {needed} is a program with a version, such as "pg_dump 17 or newer", or just "pg_restore".

data.name: Settings_PgToolsNeededVersion
data.comment: Part of the heading "pgNimbus needs …": the program and the oldest major version that works. {tool} is pg_dump; {version} is a release such as 17.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsNotFound
data.comment: Status line when the program was not found. {tool} is pg_dump or pg_restore.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsExplainDump
data.value: Backups are made by pg_dump, PostgreSQL's own backup program, which comes with pg_restore.
data.comment: Backup window, missing-program explanation: first line.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsExplainRestore
data.value: Backups are restored by pg_restore, PostgreSQL's own restore program, which comes with pg_dump.
data.comment: Restore window, missing-program explanation: first line.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsFolderProblem
data.comment: Missing-program explanation: the folder chosen in Settings holds no usable program. {folder} is a path; {reason} is a clause saying why, such as "it did not start".

data.name: Settings_PgToolsFolderNoProblem
data.comment: Missing-program explanation: the folder chosen in Settings. {folder} is a path.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsTooOld
data.value: The newest {tool} on this computer is {found}, in {folder}. This server runs PostgreSQL {server}, and {tool} has to be {version} or newer to back it up.
data.comment: Missing-program explanation: the installed program is older than the server. {tool} is pg_dump; {found} is its version, such as 15.4; {folder} is a path; {server} is the server's version, such as 17.2; {version} is the oldest major release that works, such as 17.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsNoneOnComputer
data.value: pgNimbus didn't find {tool} on this computer.
data.comment: Missing-program explanation. {tool} is pg_dump or pg_restore.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsOtherProblem
data.comment: Missing-program explanation: a program was found in a folder but does not work. {tool} is pg_dump or pg_restore; {folder} is a path; {reason} is a clause saying why.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsInstalled
data.comment: Status line of Settings, Backup and Restore: the program that will run. {tool} is pg_dump or pg_restore; {version} is its release, such as 18.6; {folder} is the folder it is in.

data.name: Settings_PgToolsInstalledFrom
data.comment: Status line of Settings, Backup and Restore: the program that will run, with what installed it. {tool} is pg_dump or pg_restore; {version} is its release, such as 18.6; {source} is the product that installed it, such as pgAdmin 4 or Homebrew; {folder} is the folder it is in.

data.name: Settings_FontInter
data.comment: Settings, Appearance tab: a choice in the Interface font list. Inter is a font name: keep it as it is.

data.name: Settings_ModifierCtrl
data.comment: Settings, General tab, Keyboard: a choice in the shortcut modifier list. A key name: keep it as it is, unless your keyboards label the key differently.

data.name: Settings_ModifierCmd
data.comment: Settings, General tab, Keyboard: a choice in the shortcut modifier list. A key name (the Command key of a Mac): keep it as it is, unless your keyboards label the key differently.

data.name: Connection_WindowTitle
data.comment: Connection dialog: the window's title (read by screen readers and the window list).

data.name: Connection_SavedConnections
data.comment: Connection dialog: heading in the title bar, over the list of saved connections.

data.name: Connection_Connect
data.comment: Connection dialog: the primary button that opens the connection, and the first item of a saved connection's right-click menu.

data.name: Connection_MenuDuplicate
data.comment: Connection dialog: right-click menu of a saved connection: makes a copy of it.

data.name: Connection_MenuDelete
data.comment: Connection dialog: right-click menu of a saved connection: deletes it after a confirmation.

data.name: Connection_ReadOnlySession
data.comment: Connection dialog: tooltip of the lock icon on a saved connection that opens read-only, and the label of the Read-only switch.

data.name: Connection_NoSavedConnections
data.value: No saved connections yet — fill in the form and it's kept here as you type
data.comment: Connection dialog: hint shown over the empty list of saved connections.

data.name: Connection_DeleteConfirm
data.value: Delete the saved connection "{name}"? Its stored password goes with it.
data.comment: Connection dialog: confirmation question before a saved connection is deleted. {name} is the connection's name, such as prod-db.

data.name: Connection_ImportPlaceholder
data.value: Paste a connection string (postgres://…, jdbc:…, Key=Value;…, psql …)
data.comment: Connection dialog: placeholder of the box that takes a pasted connection string. Keep the format examples as they are.

data.name: Connection_ImportTooltip
data.value: Paste a postgres:// URI, JDBC URL, Npgsql Key=Value string, libpq keyword string or psql command line and the fields fill in by themselves
data.comment: Connection dialog: tooltip of the paste box.

data.name: Connection_CopyTooltip
data.value: Copy the connection string without the password. Right-click to copy it with the password.
data.comment: Connection dialog: tooltip of the copy button beside the paste box.

data.name: Connection_CopyWithoutPassword
data.comment: Connection dialog: menu item of the copy button: copies the connection string with no password.

data.name: Connection_CopyWithPassword
data.comment: Connection dialog: menu item of the copy button: copies the connection string including the password.

data.name: Connection_CopyWithPasswordTooltip
data.value: Includes the password. Kept out of clipboard history where the system allows it, and cleared from the clipboard after 30 seconds.
data.comment: Connection dialog: tooltip of the Copy With Password menu item.

data.name: Connection_Name
data.comment: Connection dialog: label of the connection's name field.

data.name: Connection_AccentColorTooltip
data.value: Accent color — tints this connection's window so prod and dev are told apart at a glance
data.comment: Connection dialog: tooltip of the colour swatch button beside the name.

data.name: Connection_NoAccentColor
data.comment: Connection dialog: tooltip of the first swatch in the accent colour palette, which clears the colour.

data.name: Connection_HostPort
data.comment: Connection dialog: label over the host and port fields.

data.name: Connection_Database
data.comment: Connection dialog: label of the database name field.

data.name: Connection_Username
data.comment: Connection dialog: label of the user name field.

data.name: Connection_SslMode
data.comment: Connection dialog: label of the TLS mode picker. SSL Mode is the name of the PostgreSQL setting.

data.name: Connection_Recommended
data.comment: Connection dialog: small tag in the SSL mode list beside the mode to use.

data.name: Connection_RootCertificate
data.comment: Connection dialog: label of the field naming a certificate authority file to trust.

data.name: Connection_RootCertificatePlaceholder
data.comment: Connection dialog: placeholder of the Root Certificate field when empty.

data.name: Connection_Password
data.comment: Connection dialog: label of the database password field.

data.name: Connection_Environment
data.comment: Connection dialog: label of the picker that says whether this connection is development, staging or production.

data.name: Connection_ReadOnlyTooltip
data.value: Every statement runs in a read-only transaction, so the server refuses INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and DDL. It guards against mistakes; to make writes impossible, use a role without write privileges.
data.comment: Connection dialog: tooltip of the Read-only session switch. INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and DDL are SQL words and stay.

data.name: Connection_UseSshTunnel
data.comment: Connection dialog: label of the switch that sends the connection through an SSH server.

data.name: Connection_SshHostPort
data.comment: Connection dialog, SSH block: label over the SSH server's host and port.

data.name: Connection_SshUsername
data.comment: Connection dialog, SSH block: label of the SSH user name field.

data.name: Connection_SshAuthMethod
data.comment: Connection dialog, SSH block: label of the picker for how to sign in to the SSH server.

data.name: Connection_PrivateKeyPath
data.comment: Connection dialog, SSH block: label of the field naming the private key file.

data.name: Connection_PrivateKeyPlaceholder
data.comment: Connection dialog, SSH block: placeholder of the private key path field when empty.

data.name: Connection_SshAgentHint
data.value: Signs in with the keys your SSH agent holds, so a key with a passphrase needs nothing typed here.
data.comment: Connection dialog, SSH block: shown in place of a key field when the SSH agent method is chosen.

data.name: Connection_SshAuthAgent
data.comment: Connection dialog, SSH block: a choice of the Auth Method picker: sign in with the keys the SSH agent holds.

data.name: Connection_SshAuthKeyFile
data.comment: Connection dialog, SSH block: a choice of the Auth Method picker: sign in with a private key file.

data.name: Connection_SshAuthPassword
data.comment: Connection dialog, SSH block: a choice of the Auth Method picker: sign in with a password.

data.name: Connection_SshKeyPassphrase
data.comment: Connection dialog, SSH block: label of the field for the private key's passphrase.

data.name: Connection_SshPassword
data.comment: Connection dialog, SSH block: label of the field for the SSH account's password.

data.name: Connection_Advanced
data.comment: Connection dialog: button that opens or closes the Advanced block (client certificate and timeouts).

data.name: Connection_ClientCertificate
data.comment: Connection dialog, Advanced block: label of the field naming the client certificate file (mutual TLS).

data.name: Connection_ClientCertificatePlaceholder
data.comment: Connection dialog, Advanced block: placeholder of the client certificate field when empty. libpq is the PostgreSQL client library.

data.name: Connection_ClientKey
data.comment: Connection dialog, Advanced block: label of the field naming the client certificate's private key file.

data.name: Connection_ClientKeyPlaceholder
data.comment: Connection dialog, Advanced block: placeholder of the client key field when empty.

data.name: Connection_StatementTimeout
data.comment: Connection dialog, Advanced block: label of the field for the longest a statement may run, in seconds.

data.name: Connection_LockTimeout
data.comment: Connection dialog, Advanced block: label of the field for the longest a statement may wait for a lock, in seconds.

data.name: Connection_TimeoutNone
data.comment: Connection dialog, Advanced block: placeholder of a timeout field when empty (no timeout set).

data.name: Connection_TimeoutHint
data.value: The server cancels a statement that runs, or waits for a lock, longer than this. Empty keeps the server's and the role's own settings. Exports, imports and backups are not cut short.
data.comment: Connection dialog, Advanced block: explains the two timeout fields.

data.name: Connection_AccessingPasswordStore
data.comment: Connection dialog: shown while the operating system's credential store is being read or written.

data.name: Connection_NewConnection
data.comment: Connection dialog: tooltip and accessible name of the + button under the list that starts a new saved connection.

data.name: Connection_Test
data.comment: Connection dialog: button that tries the connection without opening it.

data.name: Connection_TestTooltip
data.value: Verify the connection (and SSH tunnel, if enabled) without opening it
data.comment: Connection dialog: tooltip of the Test button.

data.name: Connection_AboutTitle
data.comment: Connection dialog: title of the About panel that opens over the form.

data.name: Connection_PickSshKey
data.comment: Connection dialog: title of the file chooser for the SSH private key.

data.name: Connection_PickRootCertificate
data.comment: Connection dialog: title of the file chooser for the root certificate.

data.name: Connection_PickClientCertificate
data.comment: Connection dialog: title of the file chooser for the client certificate.

data.name: Connection_PickClientKey
data.comment: Connection dialog: title of the file chooser for the client key.

data.name: Connection_FileTypeCertificates
data.comment: Connection dialog: name of the certificate file filter in a file chooser.

data.name: Connection_FileTypeKeys
data.comment: Connection dialog: name of the key file filter in a file chooser.

data.name: Connection_MenuFile
data.comment: Connection dialog: macOS menu bar, the File menu while the connect window is active.

data.name: Connection_MenuCloseWindow
data.comment: Connection dialog: macOS File menu item that closes the window.

data.name: Connection_MenuEdit
data.comment: Connection dialog: macOS menu bar, the Edit menu.

data.name: Connection_MenuWindow
data.comment: Connection dialog: macOS menu bar, the Window menu.

data.name: Connection_EnvironmentHintReadOnly
data.value: Read-only session is on, so writes stay off in every window.
data.comment: Connection dialog: line under the Environment picker for a production connection that is also read-only.

data.name: Connection_SaveFailed
data.comment: Connection dialog: error line. {message} is the reason, such as Access to the path is denied.

data.name: Connection_CopyName
data.comment: Connection dialog: the name given to a duplicated connection. {name} is the original's name, such as prod-db.

data.name: Connection_TestSucceeded
data.comment: Connection dialog: status line after Test worked. {version} is the server's version, such as 17.2.

data.name: Connection_TestFailed
data.comment: Connection dialog: error line after Test failed. {message} is the reason the server or network gave.

data.name: Connection_Connecting
data.comment: Connection dialog: status line while connecting. {name} is the connection's name, such as prod-db.

data.name: Connection_ConnectFailed
data.comment: Connection dialog: error line after Connect failed. {message} is the reason the server or network gave.

data.name: Connection_SshRequired
data.value: SSH host and username are required when the tunnel is enabled.
data.comment: Connection dialog: error line when the SSH tunnel is on and its host or user is empty.

data.name: Connection_SslDisable
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode choice. The name of the PostgreSQL sslmode value 'disable'.

data.name: Connection_SslDisableHint
data.value: No encryption. Everything, the password included, is sent in the clear.
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode list: one line under the Disable choice.

data.name: Connection_SslAllow
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode choice. The name of the PostgreSQL sslmode value 'allow'.

data.name: Connection_SslAllowHint
data.value: Plaintext unless the server insists on encryption. Nothing is verified.
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode list: one line under the Allow choice.

data.name: Connection_SslPrefer
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode choice. The name of the PostgreSQL sslmode value 'prefer'.

data.name: Connection_SslPreferHint
data.value: Encrypted if the server offers it, else plaintext. An attacker can force plaintext.
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode list: one line under the Prefer choice.

data.name: Connection_SslRequire
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode choice. The name of the PostgreSQL sslmode value 'require'.

data.name: Connection_SslRequireHint
data.value: Encrypted, but the server's certificate is not checked.
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode list: one line under the Require choice.

data.name: Connection_SslVerifyCa
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode choice. The name of the PostgreSQL sslmode value 'verify-ca'. CA is certificate authority.

data.name: Connection_SslVerifyCaHint
data.value: Encrypted, and the certificate must come from a trusted CA. The host name is not checked.
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode list: one line under the Verify CA choice.

data.name: Connection_SslVerifyFull
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode choice. The name of the PostgreSQL sslmode value 'verify-full'.

data.name: Connection_SslVerifyFullHint
data.value: Encrypted, and the certificate must be trusted and name this host.
data.comment: Connection dialog: SSL Mode list: one line under the Verify full choice.

data.name: Connection_ServerWithoutTlsHint
data.value: The server does not accept TLS connections. For a local server without TLS, set SSL Mode to Prefer or Disable.

data.name: Shell_MenuExplainAnalyze
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that runs the query and shows the measured plan.

data.name: Shell_MenuFormatSql
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that reformats the SQL in the editor.

data.name: Shell_MenuExpandStar
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that replaces SELECT * with the list of column names. Keep SELECT * as it is: it is SQL.

data.name: Shell_MenuBeginTransaction
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that starts a database transaction.

data.name: Shell_MenuCommitTransaction
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that ends the open transaction and keeps its changes.

data.name: Shell_MenuRollbackTransaction
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that ends the open transaction and undoes its changes.

data.name: Shell_MenuRefreshSchema
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that reloads the schema tree from the server.

data.name: Shell_MenuServerActivity
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that opens the Server Activity window.

data.name: Shell_MenuDatabaseOverview
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that opens the Database Overview window.

data.name: Shell_MenuSlowQueries
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that opens the Slow Queries window.

data.name: Shell_MenuQueryLab
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that opens Query Lab, where saved query plans are compared.

data.name: Shell_MenuNotifyMonitor
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that opens the window that watches PostgreSQL LISTEN / NOTIFY messages. LISTEN and NOTIFY are SQL commands.

data.name: Shell_MenuRolesPermissions
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Query menu: item that opens the Roles & Permissions window.

data.name: Shell_MenuCommandPalette
data.comment: macOS menu bar, View menu: item that opens the command palette.

data.name: Shell_MenuHideSidebar
data.comment: macOS menu bar, View menu: item that hides the left sidebar. Shown while the sidebar is visible.

data.name: Shell_MenuShowSidebar
data.comment: macOS menu bar, View menu: item that shows the left sidebar. Shown while the sidebar is hidden.

data.name: Shell_MenuAppearance
data.comment: macOS menu bar, View menu: item that opens the submenu with the System, Light and Dark themes.

data.name: Shell_MenuPreviousTab
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Window menu: item that switches to the query tab on the left.

data.name: Shell_MenuNextTab
data.comment: macOS menu bar, Window menu: item that switches to the query tab on the right.

data.name: Shell_TabMenuSaveQuery
data.comment: Right-click menu of a query tab: saves the tab to the Saved Queries list. A name dialog follows.

data.name: Shell_TabMenuRename
data.comment: Right-click menu of a query tab: renames the tab in place.

data.name: Shell_TabMenuCloseOthers
data.comment: Right-click menu of a query tab: closes every other tab.

data.name: Shell_TabMenuCloseToTheRight
data.comment: Right-click menu of a query tab: closes all tabs to the right of this one.

data.name: Shell_AllowWritesConfirm
data.value: Allow writes to production ({connection}) in this window? Statements you run, grid edits, imports and schema actions can change data until you turn writes off or close the window. Other windows keep writes off.
data.comment: Confirmation dialog of the production switch in the title bar. {connection} is the connection and database, such as "prod-eu › shop". Writes are changes to data.

data.name: Shell_AllowWritesButton
data.comment: Confirmation dialog of the production switch: the red button that allows writes in this window.

data.name: Shell_ThisConnection
data.comment: Confirmation dialog of the production switch: used in place of the connection name when there is none, so it reads "Allow writes to production (this connection) in this window?".

data.name: Shell_RenameDialogTitle
data.comment: Title of the dialog that asks for a new name of a table or view (from its Maintenance menu). pgNimbus is the product name.

data.name: Shell_SwitchConnectionConfirm
data.value: Switch connection? This window closes once the new connection is open. {losses}
data.comment: Confirmation dialog of Switch Connection. {losses} is one or two sentences saying what closing the window would lose, such as "2 staged changes will be discarded."

data.name: Shell_SwitchConnectionButton
data.comment: Confirmation dialog of Switch Connection: the button that continues.

data.name: Shell_SavePlanHeading
data.comment: Heading of the dialog that names a query plan to save in Query Lab.

data.name: Shell_SavePlanTitle
data.comment: Window title of the dialog that names a query plan to save in Query Lab. pgNimbus is the product name.

data.name: Shell_PlanNotSaved
data.comment: Status line (bottom of the window): a plan could not be saved to Query Lab.

data.name: Shell_PlanSaved
data.comment: Status line (bottom of the window): a query plan was saved in Query Lab. {name} is the name the user gave it.

data.name: Shell_CloseRestoreRunning
data.value: A restore is still running, and closing this window ends its connection. Stop the restore and close? It runs as one transaction, so nothing it did stays.
data.comment: Confirmation when closing a window while a restore (pg_restore) runs.

data.name: Shell_CloseRestoreRunningLosses
data.value: A restore is still running, and closing this window ends its connection. Stop the restore and close? It runs as one transaction, so nothing it did stays. {losses}
data.comment: Confirmation when closing a window while a restore (pg_restore) runs and the window has more to lose. {losses} is one or two sentences, such as "2 staged changes will be discarded."

data.name: Shell_CloseBackupRunning
data.value: A backup is still running, and closing this window ends its connection. Stop the backup and close?
data.comment: Confirmation when closing a window while a backup (pg_dump) runs.

data.name: Shell_CloseBackupRunningLosses
data.value: A backup is still running, and closing this window ends its connection. Stop the backup and close? {losses}
data.comment: Confirmation when closing a window while a backup (pg_dump) runs and the window has more to lose. {losses} is one or two sentences, such as "2 staged changes will be discarded."

data.name: Shell_CloseWindowQuestion
data.comment: Confirmation when closing a window that would lose work. {losses} is one or two sentences, such as "2 staged changes will be discarded."

data.name: Shell_StopRestore
data.comment: Confirmation when closing a window during a restore: the red button that stops the restore and closes.

data.name: Shell_StopBackup
data.comment: Confirmation when closing a window during a backup: the red button that stops the backup and closes.

data.name: Shell_CloseWindowButton
data.comment: Confirmation when closing a window that would lose work: the red button that closes it.

data.name: Shell_StagedSummary_one
data.comment: Title line of the dialog that reviews staged changes (safe mode). Singular. {count} is how many changes, {table} the table, such as public.orders.

data.name: Shell_StagedSummary_other
data.comment: Title line of the dialog that reviews staged changes (safe mode). Plural. {count} is how many changes, such as 3; {table} the table, such as public.orders.

data.name: Shell_DiscardStagedConfirm_one
data.value: Discard {count} staged change? The database hasn't been touched.
data.comment: Confirmation of the status bar Discard button. Singular. {count} is how many staged changes.

data.name: Shell_DiscardStagedConfirm_other
data.value: Discard {count} staged changes? The database hasn't been touched.
data.comment: Confirmation of the status bar Discard button. Plural. {count} is how many staged changes, such as 3.

data.name: Shell_OpenSqlFileTitle
data.comment: Title of the system file picker that opens a .sql file.

data.name: Shell_SaveSqlFileTitle
data.comment: Title of the system file picker that saves a .sql file.

data.name: Shell_AllFiles
data.comment: File picker: name of the file type filter that shows every file.

data.name: Shell_CantOpenNonLocal
data.comment: Status line: the chosen file is not on this computer (for example a cloud location) and cannot be opened.

data.name: Shell_OpenFailed
data.comment: Status line: a .sql file could not be read. {error} is the system error text, such as "Access to the path is denied."

data.name: Shell_FileNotFound
data.comment: Status line: a recent file no longer exists. {path} is its full path.

data.name: Shell_CantSaveNonLocal
data.value: Can't save to a non-local file
data.comment: Status line: the chosen location is not on this computer and cannot be written.

data.name: Shell_SavedFile
data.comment: Status line: a .sql file was written. {file} is the file name, such as report.sql.

data.name: Shell_SaveFailed
data.comment: Status line: a .sql file could not be written. {error} is the system error text.

data.name: Shell_NothingToSave
data.value: Nothing to save: this tab is empty
data.comment: Status line: Save was used on a tab with no text.

data.name: Shell_SavedQuery
data.comment: Status line: the tab was saved in the Saved Queries list. {name} is the name of the saved query.

data.name: Shell_SaveAsNewQueryHeading
data.comment: Heading of the dialog that names a new saved query (Save As).

data.name: Shell_SaveQueryHeading
data.comment: Heading of the dialog that names a saved query.

data.name: Shell_FiltersNeedBrowse
data.value: Filters apply while browsing a table: double-click one in the sidebar. A query you wrote is never rewritten; add a WHERE to it instead.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: shown when the filter command is used outside a browsed table. WHERE is the SQL keyword.

data.name: Shell_AutoAliasOn
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: auto-alias was switched on. The example shows what it does to SQL: the table name orders gets the alias o.

data.name: Shell_AutoAliasOff
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: auto-alias was switched off.

data.name: Shell_SafeModeOn
data.value: Safe mode: on — grid edits, deletes, and inserts are staged for review
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: safe mode was switched on. Safe mode holds changes back for review before they reach the database.

data.name: Shell_SafeModeOff
data.value: Safe mode: off — grid changes apply immediately
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: safe mode was switched off.

data.name: Shell_NoPlanOnScreen
data.value: No plan on screen: run Explain or Explain Analyze, or import a plan, first
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a plan command (save or compare) was used while no query plan is shown.

data.name: Shell_CantSwitchDatabase
data.value: This window can't switch databases: it has no connection profile to open another database with.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: the Switch database command was used in a window that has no saved connection profile.

data.name: Shell_SwitchDatabaseConfirm
data.comment: Confirmation dialog when switching database. {database} is the database name; {losses} is one or two sentences saying what closing the current connection would lose, such as "2 staged changes will be discarded."

data.name: Shell_SwitchDatabaseButton
data.comment: Confirmation dialog when switching database: the button that continues.

data.name: Shell_StayedOn
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: the database switch was declined. {database} is the current database.

data.name: Shell_ConnectingTo
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a connection to another database is being opened. {database} is its name.

data.name: Shell_OpenDatabaseFailed
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: connecting to another database failed. {database} is its name; {error} is the error text, such as "permission denied for database".

data.name: Shell_LossStaged_one
data.comment: One item in the list of what closing a connection loses (joined into a sentence by the app). Singular. A sentence fragment starting in lowercase or with a number. {count} is how many changes staged in safe mode.

data.name: Shell_LossStaged_other
data.comment: One item in the list of what closing a connection loses. Plural. {count} is how many changes staged in safe mode, such as 3.

data.name: Shell_LossTransaction
data.value: the open transaction will be rolled back
data.comment: One item in the list of what closing a connection loses (joined into a sentence by the app). A sentence fragment starting in lowercase.

data.name: Shell_LossRunning_one
data.value: the running query will be cancelled
data.comment: One item in the list of what closing a connection loses. Singular: one query is running. A sentence fragment starting in lowercase.

data.name: Shell_LossRunning_other
data.comment: One item in the list of what closing a connection loses. Plural. {count} is how many queries are running, such as 2.

data.name: Shell_LossesTwo
data.comment: Joins two items of the list of what closing a connection loses into one phrase. {first} and {second} are fragments such as "the open transaction will be rolled back".

data.name: Shell_LossesThree
data.comment: Joins three items of the list of what closing a connection loses into one phrase. Each is a fragment such as "the open transaction will be rolled back".

data.name: Shell_LossesSentence
data.comment: Ends the list of what closing a connection loses as a sentence. {losses} is the joined phrase; the app capitalizes its first letter.

data.name: Shell_RestoreNeedsConnection
data.value: Restoring needs a connection that pg_restore can use, and this window has none.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: Restore Backup was used in a window with no connection profile. pg_restore is PostgreSQL's program and keeps its name.

data.name: Shell_RestoreReadOnly
data.value: This connection is read-only, so it can't restore a backup. Connect with a profile that can write.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: Restore Backup was used on a read-only connection.

data.name: Shell_BackupNeedsConnection
data.value: Backups need a connection that pg_dump can use, and this window has none.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: Back Up Database was used in a window with no connection profile. pg_dump is PostgreSQL's program and keeps its name.

data.name: Shell_ReadOnlySessionHint
data.value: the connection is read-only, so the server refuses writes.
data.comment: The reason a connection cannot write, shown after "Read-only: " in a tooltip and as the reason a grid cannot be edited. A sentence fragment starting in lowercase.

data.name: Shell_ProductionLockedHint
data.value: this is a production connection, and writes are off in this window until you allow them.
data.comment: The reason a production connection cannot write yet, shown in tooltips after "Read-only: " or "Results are read-only: ". A sentence fragment starting in lowercase.

data.name: Shell_ProductionNotEnforcedHint
data.value: writes should be off on this production connection, but the server or a connection pooler did not apply that option, and the server accepts writes. pgNimbus keeps the grid read-only, but only pgNimbus blocks writes now: SQL you run can still change data.
data.comment: Tooltip reason of the amber read-only warning on a production connection whose server did not apply the read-only option. A sentence fragment starting in lowercase. pgNimbus is the product name.

data.name: Shell_ReadOnlyNotEnforcedHint
data.value: the profile asks for a read-only connection, but the server or a connection pooler did not apply that option, and the server accepts writes. pgNimbus keeps the grid read-only, but only pgNimbus blocks writes now: SQL you run can still change data. Don't rely on this profile's protection in this session.
data.comment: Tooltip reason of the amber read-only warning on a connection profile marked read-only whose server did not apply the option. A sentence fragment starting in lowercase. pgNimbus is the product name.

data.name: Shell_ReadOnlyNotApplied_Status
data.value: Read-only was not applied: the server or a connection pooler ignored the profile's read-only option. The grid stays read-only, but SQL you run can write.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: the connection should be read-only but the server accepts writes.

data.name: Shell_StandbyHint
data.value: the server is a standby replica, which refuses writes.
data.comment: The reason a connection cannot write, shown after "Read-only: " in a tooltip. A sentence fragment starting in lowercase. A standby replica is a read-only copy of a PostgreSQL server.

data.name: Shell_WritesToggleOn
data.value: Production: writes are allowed in this window. Click to turn them off.
data.comment: Tooltip of the production switch in the title bar while writes are allowed.

data.name: Shell_WritesToggleOff
data.value: Production: writes are off in this window, and the server refuses them. Click to allow writes for this window.
data.comment: Tooltip of the production switch in the title bar while writes are off.

data.name: Shell_ProductionProfileReadOnly
data.value: This production profile is read-only, so its windows can't allow writes. Turn off Read-only session in the profile.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: the production switch was used on a production profile that is read-only. "Read-only session" is the name of an option in the connection dialog.

data.name: Shell_OnlyProductionToggles
data.value: Only a production profile's window turns writes on and off.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a command for the production write switch was used in a window that is not a production window.

data.name: Shell_WritesAllowedStatus
data.value: Writes are allowed in this window. Other windows on this profile still have them off.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: writes were allowed in this production window.

data.name: Shell_CommitFirst
data.value: Commit or roll back the open transaction first: it holds a connection that can write.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: writes cannot be turned off while a transaction is open.

data.name: Shell_WritesOffAgain
data.value: Writes are off in this window again.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: writes were turned off again in this production window.

data.name: Shell_SignalsLockedHint
data.value: Writes are off in this production window, so it doesn't cancel or terminate other sessions. Allow writes first.
data.comment: Server Activity window: tooltip explaining why the Cancel query and Terminate buttons are disabled in a production window while writes are off.

data.name: Shell_WordWrapOn
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: word wrap in the SQL editor was switched on.

data.name: Shell_WordWrapOff
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: word wrap in the SQL editor was switched off.

data.name: Shell_ImportedPlanUnreadable
data.value: The imported plan could not be read back. Import it again with Import query plan…
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a tab holding an imported query plan could not restore its plan after the app restarted. "Import query plan…" is the name of a command.

data.name: Shell_CompletionCatalogStale
data.value: Autocomplete kept the previous catalog: refresh failed ({error})
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: reloading the names for autocomplete failed. {error} is the error text.

data.name: Shell_TransactionStarted
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a transaction was started. BEGIN is the SQL command and stays.

data.name: Shell_TransactionBeginFailed
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: starting a transaction failed. {error} is the error text.

data.name: Shell_TransactionCommitted
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: the transaction was committed. COMMIT is the SQL command and stays.

data.name: Shell_TransactionCommitFailed
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: committing the transaction failed. {error} is the error text.

data.name: Shell_TransactionRolledBack
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: the transaction was rolled back. ROLLBACK is the SQL command and stays.

data.name: Shell_TransactionRollbackFailed
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: rolling back the transaction failed. {error} is the error text.

data.name: Shell_TabSourceTitle
data.comment: Name of the tab that shows the CREATE statement of a table or function. {name} is the table or function name, such as orders. Keep the dot.

data.name: Shell_TabNewTableTitle
data.comment: Name of the tab that holds a CREATE TABLE template for a schema. {schema} is the schema name, such as public. Keep the dot.

data.name: Shell_ImportedPlanTitle
data.comment: Name of the tab that shows a query plan imported from pasted text.

data.name: Shell_SelectTableFirst
data.value: Select a table in the schema tree, or browse one, first.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a table command (analyze, vacuum, truncate, rename, drop) was used with no table selected.

data.name: Shell_MaintVerb_Analyze
data.comment: The verb "analyze" (lowercase, the base form) used inside the messages "Can't analyze …" and "Couldn't analyze …" about the ANALYZE command on a table.

data.name: Shell_MaintVerb_Vacuum
data.comment: The verb "vacuum" (lowercase, the base form) used inside the messages "Can't vacuum …" and "Couldn't vacuum …" about the VACUUM command on a table.

data.name: Shell_MaintVerb_Truncate
data.comment: The verb "truncate" (lowercase, the base form) used inside the messages "Can't truncate …" and "Couldn't truncate …" about emptying a table.

data.name: Shell_MaintVerb_Rename
data.comment: The verb "rename" (lowercase, the base form) used inside the messages "Can't rename …" and "Couldn't rename …" about renaming a table.

data.name: Shell_MaintVerb_Drop
data.comment: The verb "drop" (lowercase, the base form) used inside the messages "Can't drop …" and "Couldn't drop …" about deleting a table.

data.name: Shell_MaintCantApply
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a table command does not apply to this kind of object. {verb} is the verb, such as truncate; {table} is schema.name; {noun} is view or materialized view.

data.name: Shell_MaintCantReason
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a table command was refused. {verb} is the verb, such as drop; {table} is schema.name; {reason} is a sentence that says why, such as "the connection is read-only, so the server refuses writes."

data.name: Shell_InDatabase
data.comment: Fragment placed inside the Truncate and Drop confirmations, after the table name, with a leading space: " in database "shop"". {database} is the database name.

data.name: Shell_TruncateEffectPartitioned
data.value: Every row in it and in all its partitions is deleted
data.comment: Part of the Truncate confirmation, for a partitioned table. A sentence without its final period; the confirmation continues with ", and this can't be undone."

data.name: Shell_TruncateEffect
data.value: Every row in it is deleted
data.comment: Part of the Truncate confirmation, for an ordinary table. A sentence without its final period; the confirmation continues with ", and this can't be undone."

data.name: Shell_TruncateConfirm
data.value: Truncate table "{table}"{database}? {effect}, and this can't be undone. It fails if another table's foreign key references it.
data.comment: Confirmation of Truncate in a table's Maintenance menu. {table} is schema.name; {database} is the fragment " in database "shop"" (or empty); {effect} is a phrase such as "Every row in it is deleted".

data.name: Shell_TruncateButton
data.comment: Confirmation of Truncate: the red button that empties the table.

data.name: Shell_DropEffectView
data.comment: Part of the Drop confirmation, for a view. A sentence without its final period; the confirmation continues with ", and this can't be undone."

data.name: Shell_DropEffectMaterializedView
data.value: The materialized view and its data are removed
data.comment: Part of the Drop confirmation, for a materialized view. A sentence without its final period.

data.name: Shell_DropEffectPartitioned
data.value: The table and all its partitions, with every row in them, are removed
data.comment: Part of the Drop confirmation, for a partitioned table. A sentence without its final period.

data.name: Shell_DropEffectTable
data.value: The table and every row in it are removed
data.comment: Part of the Drop confirmation, for an ordinary table. A sentence without its final period.

data.name: Shell_DropConfirm
data.value: Drop {noun} "{table}"{database}? {effect}, and this can't be undone. It fails if a view or another table's foreign key depends on it.
data.comment: Confirmation of Drop in a table's Maintenance menu. {noun} is table, view or materialized view; {table} is schema.name; {database} is the fragment " in database "shop"" (or empty); {effect} is a phrase such as "The view is removed".

data.name: Shell_DropButton
data.comment: Confirmation of Drop: the red button that deletes the table or view.

data.name: Shell_RenameHeading
data.comment: Heading of the dialog that asks for a new name. {noun} is table, view or materialized view; {table} is schema.name.

data.name: Shell_MaintRunningAnalyze
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: ANALYZE is running. {table} is schema.name.

data.name: Shell_MaintRunningVacuum
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: VACUUM is running. {table} is schema.name.

data.name: Shell_MaintRunningTruncate
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a table is being emptied. {table} is schema.name.

data.name: Shell_MaintRunningRename
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a table is being renamed. {table} is schema.name.

data.name: Shell_MaintRunningDrop
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a table is being deleted. {table} is schema.name.

data.name: Shell_MaintFailed
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a table command failed. {verb} is the verb, such as drop; {table} is schema.name; {error} is the server error text.

data.name: Shell_MaintDoneAnalyze
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: ANALYZE finished. {table} is schema.name; {seconds} is the duration, such as 0.4. s means seconds.

data.name: Shell_MaintDoneVacuum
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: VACUUM finished. {table} is schema.name; {seconds} is the duration, such as 0.4. s means seconds.

data.name: Shell_MaintDoneTruncate
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a table was emptied. {table} is schema.name.

data.name: Shell_MaintDoneRename
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a table was renamed. {table} is the old schema.name; {newName} is the new schema.name.

data.name: Shell_MaintDoneDrop
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a table was deleted. {table} is schema.name.

data.name: Shell_SchemaExcluded
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a schema was left out of autocomplete. {schema} is the schema name.

data.name: Shell_SchemaIncluded
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a schema was put back into autocomplete. {schema} is the schema name.

data.name: Shell_ReopenedTab
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a closed tab was brought back. {title} is its name.

data.name: Shell_ClosedUnsaved_one
data.value: Closed “{title}”, which had unsaved SQL. {how} reopens it.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: a tab with unsaved SQL was closed. Singular. {title} is the tab name; {how} is the shortcut that brings it back (such as Ctrl+Shift+T) or the command name "Reopen closed tab".

data.name: Shell_ClosedUnsaved_other
data.value: Closed {count} tabs with unsaved SQL. {how} reopens them one at a time.
data.comment: Status line at the bottom of the main window: several tabs with unsaved SQL were closed. Plural. {count} is how many, such as 3; {how} is the shortcut that brings them back (such as Ctrl+Shift+T) or the command name "Reopen closed tab".

data.name: Shell_PaletteAction
data.comment: Command palette: grey category label at the right end of a row that runs a command.

data.name: Shell_PaletteSavedQuery
data.comment: Command palette: grey category label at the right end of a row that opens a saved query.

data.name: Shell_PaletteRecentFile
data.comment: Command palette: grey category label at the right end of a row that opens a recently used .sql file.

data.name: Shell_PaletteTable
data.comment: Command palette: grey category label at the right end of a row that opens a table (also used for views).

data.name: Shell_SearchMatchCaseLabel
data.comment: Find bar of the SQL editor (also of the cell inspector), top right of the editor: the short label on the Match case toggle: the same letter in upper and lower case. Adapt to the script of the language if "Aa" means nothing there.

data.name: Shell_SearchWholeWordsLabel
data.comment: Find bar of the SQL editor (also of the cell inspector), top right of the editor: the short label on the Whole words toggle, drawn underlined: a word. Adapt to the script of the language if "ab" means nothing there.

data.name: Sidebar_NewTable

data.name: Security_DefaultAclNote
data.value: No GRANT or REVOKE has ever been run on this object. {owner} owns it and holds every privilege; everyone else has only what Postgres grants by default for this object type.
data.comment: Permissions tab: banner shown when the object's privileges were never changed. GRANT and REVOKE are SQL. {owner} is the owning role's name, such as postgres.

data.name: Security_CellTip
data.comment: Permissions tab: tooltip of a cell of the matrix. {privilege} is the SQL privilege such as SELECT; {explanation} says why the role has it or not, such as inherited from readers.

data.name: Security_CellTipPendingRevoke
data.comment: Permissions tab: second line of a cell's tooltip when a REVOKE is staged for it. REVOKE is SQL.

data.name: Security_CellTipPendingGrant
data.comment: Permissions tab: second line of a cell's tooltip when a GRANT is staged for it. GRANT is SQL.

data.name: Security_CellTipNotRevocable
data.value: Ownership and superuser are not grants, so this cannot be revoked.
data.comment: Permissions tab: second line of a cell's tooltip when the privilege comes from owning the object or being a superuser.

data.name: Security_SourceSuperuser
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the role has everything because it is a superuser.

data.name: Security_SourceOwner
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the role has everything because it owns the object.

data.name: Security_SourceVia
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the role has the privileges through its membership in another role. {role} is that group role, such as readers.

data.name: Security_SourceDirect
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the privilege was granted to the role itself.

data.name: Security_SourcePublic
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the privilege was granted to PUBLIC, the SQL keyword for every role. A translation may keep it.

data.name: Security_SourceUnknown
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the server says the role has the privilege but the catalog does not show why.

data.name: Security_PublicGrantee
data.comment: The grantee shown for a privilege or policy that applies to every role: the SQL keyword PUBLIC. A translation may keep it. A role that is merely named PUBLIC is shown in quotation marks by the app, so the two can be told apart.

data.name: Security_ExplainNone
data.comment: Why a role does or does not have a privilege (tooltip of a matrix cell, and part of the sentence under the matrix): it was not granted.

data.name: Security_ExplainDirectBy
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it was granted to the role itself. {grantor} is the role that ran the GRANT, such as postgres.

data.name: Security_ExplainDirect
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it was granted to the role itself, by a role we cannot name.

data.name: Security_ExplainInherited
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: through its membership in a group role. {role} is that group, such as readers.

data.name: Security_ExplainPublic
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it was granted to PUBLIC, the SQL keyword for every role.

data.name: Security_ExplainOwner
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it owns the object.

data.name: Security_ExplainSuperuser
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it is a superuser.

data.name: Security_ExplainUnknown
data.value: granted, source not visible from here
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: the server says yes but the catalog the app can read does not explain it.

data.name: Security_ListSeparator
data.comment: Separator between the items of a list of privileges, such as SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE. Put a space after it if your language uses one.

data.name: Security_ListAnd
data.comment: Joins a list of privileges with and: {head} is the items before the last one, joined by the list separator (SELECT, INSERT), {last} is the last one (UPDATE).

data.name: Security_ListOr
data.comment: Joins a list of privileges with or: {head} is the items before the last one, joined by the list separator (SELECT, INSERT), {last} is the last one (UPDATE).

data.name: Security_SentenceNone
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. {role} is a role name, {object} the object such as sales.orders.

data.name: Security_SentenceNoneBlocked
data.value: {role} has no privileges on {object}. {role} also lacks USAGE on schema {schema}, which blocks access to everything in it.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. {role} is a role name, {object} the object such as sales.orders, {schema} its schema. USAGE is a SQL privilege name.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlocked_one
data.value: {role} holds {privileges} on {object} — {explanation} — but cannot use it: it lacks USAGE on schema {schema}, which every object in it needs first.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Singular: one privilege is held but unusable. {role} is a role name, {privileges} the privilege such as SELECT, {object} the object, {explanation} why the role has it, {schema} the schema. "it" is the privilege. USAGE is a SQL privilege name.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlocked_other
data.value: {role} holds {privileges} on {object} — {explanation} — but cannot use them: it lacks USAGE on schema {schema}, which every object in it needs first.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Plural: several privileges are held but unusable. {role} is a role name, {privileges} a list such as SELECT and INSERT, {object} the object, {explanation} why the role has them, {schema} the schema. "them" is the privileges. USAGE is a SQL privilege name.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlockedDenied_one
data.value: {role} holds {privileges} on {object} — {explanation} — but cannot use it: it lacks USAGE on schema {schema}, which every object in it needs first. It has no {denied} grant either.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Singular: one privilege is held but unusable, and others are missing. Same placeholders as Security_SentenceBlocked_one, plus {denied}, the missing privileges as a list joined with or, such as INSERT or UPDATE.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlockedDenied_other
data.value: {role} holds {privileges} on {object} — {explanation} — but cannot use them: it lacks USAGE on schema {schema}, which every object in it needs first. It has no {denied} grant either.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Plural: several privileges are held but unusable, and others are missing. Same placeholders as Security_SentenceBlocked_other, plus {denied}, the missing privileges as a list joined with or, such as INSERT or UPDATE.

data.name: Security_SentenceCan
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. {role} is a role name, {privileges} what it can do as SQL verbs such as SELECT and INSERT, {object} the object such as sales.orders, {explanation} why, such as inherited from readers.

data.name: Security_SentenceCanCannot
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Same placeholders as Security_SentenceCan, plus {denied}, what the role cannot do as a list joined with or, such as INSERT or UPDATE.

data.value: Open the ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statement this row represents in a new editor tab
data.comment: Default privileges tab: tooltip of the Copy as SQL button. ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES is SQL.

data.name: Security_ColCreatedBy
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the role that will create the objects the default applies to.

data.name: Security_ColInSchema
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the schema the default applies in.

data.name: Security_ColAppliesTo

data.name: Security_ColGrantee
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the role that gets the privileges.

data.name: Security_ColPrivileges
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the list of privileges.

data.name: Security_AllSchemas
data.comment: Shown instead of a schema name in the Default privileges tab (the default applies in every schema) and as the first choice of the schema filter in the Row-level security tab. Keep the parentheses.

data.name: Security_AppliesToTables
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to tables.

data.name: Security_AppliesToSequences
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to sequences.

data.name: Security_AppliesToFunctions
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to functions.

data.name: Security_AppliesToTypes
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to data types.

data.name: Security_AppliesToSchemas
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to schemas.

data.name: Security_NoDefaultPrivileges
data.comment: Default privileges tab: heading shown when there are none.

data.name: Security_NoDefaultPrivilegesHint
data.value: Every object created from now on will carry only the built-in defaults: its owner gets everything, PUBLIC gets EXECUTE on functions and USAGE on types, and nothing at all on tables and sequences.
data.comment: Default privileges tab: explanation under the heading shown when there are none. PUBLIC, EXECUTE and USAGE are SQL words and stay as written.

data.name: Security_DefaultsNoteExisting
data.value: These do not affect objects that already exist. They apply to objects created from now on, which is why a GRANT … ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA … and a default privilege are both needed: neither replaces the other.
data.comment: Default privileges tab: first note under the list. The GRANT statement is SQL and stays as written.

data.name: Security_DefaultsNoteCreator
data.value: They are keyed to the role that creates the object, not to the schema it lands in. A default privilege set for the wrong creator runs fine and silently does nothing — the single most common reason someone says they set default privileges and nothing changed.
data.comment: Default privileges tab: second note under the list.

data.name: Security_DefaultPrivilegesTabTitle
data.comment: Title of the query tab that opens with an ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statement. {owner} is the role that creates the objects, such as app_rw.

data.name: Security_SchemaFilterTip
data.value: Only schemas that have row-level security anywhere are listed
data.comment: Row-level security tab: tooltip of the schema filter.

data.name: Security_CopyPolicyAsSql
data.comment: Row-level security tab: button that opens the selected policy's CREATE POLICY statement in a new query tab.

data.name: Security_CopyPolicyAsSqlTip
data.value: Open the selected policy's CREATE POLICY statement in a new editor tab — Postgres cannot change a policy's command or permissiveness in place, so re-creating it is how one gets edited
data.comment: Row-level security tab: tooltip of the Copy policy as SQL button. CREATE POLICY is SQL.

data.name: Security_PoliciesInert
data.comment: Row-level security tab, list of tables: warning on a table that has policies but row-level security is switched off. RLS means row-level security.

data.name: Security_PoliciesDoNothing
data.comment: Row-level security tab: heading of a warning about a table whose policies have no effect.

data.name: Security_PoliciesDoNothingHint
data.value: Row-level security was never switched on for this table, so every policy below is inert and every role reads every row. Writing policies does not enable it — ALTER TABLE … ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY does.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: explanation of the warning. The ALTER TABLE statement is SQL and stays as written.

data.name: Security_YouBypass
data.comment: Row-level security tab: heading of a warning that the connected role is not subject to the policies.

data.name: Security_DeniesEverything
data.value: Row-level security is enabled and this table has no policies, so it returns no rows to any role that does not bypass it. That is the default-deny state, not a misconfiguration in itself.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: note on a table with row-level security on and no policies.

data.name: Security_PolicyAppliesTo
data.comment: Row-level security tab: label before the roles a policy applies to.

data.name: Security_PolicyUsing
data.value: USING — which existing rows are visible
data.comment: Row-level security tab: label above a policy's USING expression. USING is the SQL keyword and stays first.

data.name: Security_PolicyWithCheck
data.value: WITH CHECK — which new or updated rows are allowed
data.comment: Row-level security tab: label above a policy's WITH CHECK expression. WITH CHECK is the SQL keyword and stays first.

data.name: Security_NoPolicies
data.comment: Row-level security tab: shown in the details of a table without policies.

data.name: Security_NoRlsTables
data.value: No table here uses row-level security.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: heading shown when no table has row-level security or a policy.

data.name: Security_NoRlsTablesHint
data.value: Tables appear here as soon as they have row security enabled or carry a policy, in either order.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: explanation under the heading shown when no table has row-level security.

data.name: Security_RlsEnabledForce
data.comment: Row-level security tab: state of a table. Row-level security is on and also applies to the table's owner (SQL option FORCE).

data.name: Security_RlsEnabled
data.comment: Row-level security tab: state of a table. Row-level security is on.

data.name: Security_RlsNotEnabled
data.comment: Row-level security tab: state of a table. Row-level security is off.

data.name: Security_PolicyCount_one
data.comment: Row-level security tab: how many policies a table has. Singular.

data.name: Security_PolicyCount_other
data.comment: Row-level security tab: how many policies a table has. Plural. {count} is the number, such as 3.

data.name: Security_PolicyForEveryone
data.comment: Row-level security tab: the policy applies to every role (the SQL keyword PUBLIC).

data.name: Security_BypassUnknown
data.value: {role} sees every row in this table, whatever the policies below say. Its role attributes could not be read, so this is either a superuser or BYPASSRLS role (which bypasses every table, always) or ownership of a table that is not FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. BYPASSRLS and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY are SQL and stay as written.

data.name: Security_BypassSuperuser
data.value: {role} is a superuser, so it bypasses row-level security on every table in the cluster. That is unconditional: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY does not apply the policies to it. Test these policies as the role your application connects as.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is SQL and stays as written.

data.name: Security_BypassAttribute
data.value: {role} has the BYPASSRLS attribute, so it bypasses row-level security on every table, always. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY does not apply the policies to it. Test these policies as the role your application connects as.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. BYPASSRLS and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY are SQL and stay as written.

data.name: Security_BypassOwner
data.value: {role} owns this table, or is a member of the role that does, and the table is not FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY — so the policies below are not applied to it, though they are applied to every other role. ALTER TABLE … FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY makes them apply to the owner too.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the ALTER TABLE statement are SQL and stay as written.

data.name: Security_ObjectDropped
data.value: {object} no longer exists — it was dropped since the object list was built.
data.comment: Error line of the Roles and Permissions window. {object} is the name of the object, such as sales.orders.
